candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the appropriate timing and purpose of rapid response activation.

options.A: Bring additional clinical expertise to the bedside for immediate assessment and treatment before deterioration progresses to arrest.
options.B: Wait until the client has no pulse before calling for additional help.
options.C: Transfer responsibility permanently away from the primary nurse.
options.D: Use the system only for clients already located in an intensive care unit.

candidate.rationale: Rapid response systems are designed for signs of clinical deterioration before a full cardiopulmonary arrest. A rapid response team comes to the bedside to assess and treat the patient promptly with the goal of preventing further deterioration and serious adverse outcomes.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Rapid response systems provide early bedside assessment and treatment for deteriorating patients before arrest.
candidate.source_locator: Rapid response team—bedside assessment/treatment for signs of deterioration before cardiac arrest
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, PSNet
candidate.stem: A hospitalized client develops new tachypnea, increasing confusion, and a falling blood pressure but has not had a cardiac arrest. What is the purpose of activating a rapid response system at this point?
